newsitem.title: USA: U.S. exchanges eyeing trading in decimal pricing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. exchanges eyeing trading in decimal pricing.

text.p: U.S. stock exchanges and the Nasdaq market are eyeing quoting and trading of stocks priced in decimals rather than fractions.

The National Association of Securities Dealers Inc (NASD) said in a news release Tuesday it was seeking comment from investors and industry representatives and Nasdaq companies on the impact of a change to decimals.

A source familiar with the situation said the New York Stock Exchange board of directors, at its regular monthly meeting Thursday, will consider the issues of both decimalization and pricing in smaller fractions than are used now.
Except for a handful of very low-priced issues, the smallest fraction used at the NYSE is 1/8.
A New York Stock Exchange spokesman declined comment.

"We think it is inevitable," said a spokesman for the American Stock Exchange when asked about a possible change to decimal pricing. "We will do it when the industry is ready. clearly we support the objective which is smaller increments."
She said last week ago the Amex began trading in increments of 1/16.
Nasdaq implemented quotation increments of 1/16 for securities with bid prices of $10 or above on June 2.

Industry analysts have said the smaller increments, whether as a result of decimalization or smaller fractions, result in smaller "spreads" between bid and asked prices which means better prices for investors. The smaller spreads also could hurt profits of brokerage firms, analysts have said.
